items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation. Calvin asked 'how are you?' and then answered his own question — 'Yeah, I'm, well, yeah, we don't, we don't charge a deposit or anything to book' — never letting Zoe respond and never setting a roadmap for the call.
Customer's name was never spoken once. She used his twice ('Hi Calvin! How are you?' and 'Thank you Calvin for following up') and he never reciprocated with 'Zoe' at any point in 6.5 minutes.

Hourly rate was never stated. Calvin referred to 'that rate' and 'part of the hourly rate' three separate times without ever saying the dollar figure, the per-mover-per-hour structure, or day-of-week tiers — on a follow-up call whose entire purpose was to convert a live quote.

Number of movers and trucks never stated, and no typical time range for her home size was given. The customer materially downsized the inventory on this call — 'I do not have that much furniture. Is a bed and then the co, the cabinets. And then, and then sofa' plus 'I don't have appliances, I don't have, yeah, TV and then nothing' — and Calvin never revisited the estimate against the lighter load. That is both a closing miss and an estimate-accuracy risk.

No Worries Damage Coverage never named and the $2,000 figure never stated. Zoe raised fragile goods directly — 'the photo framework, the lots of mirrors and the glasses and those kind of a dedicate' — and the answer was 'it's fully insured as well' plus a garbled 'the insurance that hire evaluation that we provide.' The strongest available differentiator went unused on a perfectly teed-up objection.

Meet Your Mover never mentioned — the single most glaring miss on this call. Zoe explicitly asked for it: 'the current location is a gated community and I will need the driver's name and the poppy, the your trucks Li, license number' and 'give me like a one day, two days in advance so that I have to inform the landlord.' Calvin's reply was 'we would be able to get that once it was booked so we would know what truck it was on and who the driver was going to be' — describing Meet Your Mover without naming it, and framing it as something she'd have to chase rather than a standard email that arrives a few days out. Naming it there was a closing lever.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, despite Calvin quoting a specific arrival window — '8:30 AM to 9:00 AM arrival is still available.' The window was stated with no guarantee attached to it.

Packing services never offered. Zoe flagged the pain herself twice: 'boxes that I will take a lot of time to put, put up everything' and 'I'm very, very busy this recent days.' Neither the packing service nor its pricing (same hourly rate plus materials) was raised. Direct revenue miss on a stated pain point.
Box count never asked, and no Ecobox referral made even though she volunteered that boxing everything up would consume her time.

Clock section almost entirely missing. Calvin got the on-site start right — 'you sign and then the, they start the clock' — but never gave the 2.5-hour minimum, never explained 15-minute prorated increments ('it does the math automatically' was as far as it went), and never sense-checked with 'does that make sense?'

Save Your Ass section: zero. No mention that prep before move day shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls), and no 'take a carload' tip. Zoe actually opened the door — 'the computer, I will take my my P-C's' — and the response was 'Mm-hmm.' On a follow-up call for a small, box-heavy self-pack move, this was the highest-value 90 seconds available and it never happened.
No moving-stressor question. 'I'm very, very busy this recent days' and the gated-community access worry both went un-probed as stressors.
Stairs/floors and parking/truck access at either address never confirmed, even after she raised the gated community herself.

Booking close never completed. Calvin built real urgency — 'it is a Saturday, those are popular days... we might end up booking that out' — but when she said 'let me, let me just think for a while' and 'I'll get back to you as soon as possible,' he accepted it with 'Okay, sounds good. Well, let us know' and never proposed a specific callback time or offered to soft-hold the 9/12 slot.

Email specifics missed: no BOLDED-details-at-the-top framing and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask — even though a confirmation email was offered ('I can send a confirmation email and you have the spot held').
'Any other questions before I let you go?' never asked, and business hours / how to reach us never given — on a call that ended with the customer holding an open decision.

Trip fee discount given away with nothing asked in return. She asked 'is there any room to negotiate?' and Calvin went straight to $210 → $150, then confirmed 'I've updated that in the booking' before she committed to anything. The concession was banked into the record while the close stayed open.
top_strength: Calvin's FAQ and trust-building work was genuinely strong, and it is why this call ended warm despite no booking. He led with the friction-removers unprompted and repeated them at exactly the right moments: 'we don't charge a deposit or anything to book and, and we don't take credit cards in advance,' then 'there's no deposit to book, there's no rescheduling or cancellation fee, you know, we don't, we don't charge anything.' When she asked how payment actually works, he walked the whole mechanic clearly — the on-site iPad, signing the proposal and trip fee, 'they start the clock you can see the movers even like, hey, okay, I see what time it started when the move is done they stop the time,' Clover Go on Bank of America, tap-to-pay, and the reassurance that 'no credit card information gets stored. The last four is always like visible but that's about it.' He also caught and answered her live anxiety about the lease deposit she'd just paid — 'there is no deposit or cancellation rescheduling fee. So, yeah, if you do end up booking and anything changes you don't, you don't need to worry about like, you know, like with your lease where if that you know, you already paid a deposit.' On the negotiation he held the floor without getting defensive and justified it on quality rather than apologizing: 'we can't decrease it much because of you know we pay, we have like the best movers we pay them really well. We background check everyone and they're trained by us.' The customer closed the call with 'Thank you Calvin for following up' — earned.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: Zoe handed Calvin Meet Your Mover on a platter and he answered it as a logistics chore instead of a differentiator. When she said she needed the driver's name and truck plate a day or two ahead for the gated community, the line was: 'Zoe, that's already built in — it's called Meet Your Mover. A few days before your move you'll get an email with your mover's photo and basic info plus the truck details, so you'll have everything you need to send to your landlord well before the twelfth. Nothing for you to chase.' That single answer converts an objection into a reason to book, and it was the natural close on this call. Second priority: stop paying for the booking before you have it. She asked 'is there any room to negotiate?' and the trip fee dropped $60 and was written into the record — 'I've updated that in the booking' — while the decision stayed open, so the concession bought nothing. Trade it instead: 'I can do $150 total on the trip fee — $75 each way — if we lock the twelfth in right now. Want me to send that confirmation?' Third: the Save Your Ass speech was completely absent on the ideal call for it. Small self-pack load, box-heavy, customer already telling you she's short on time — 'the more you can have boxed and consolidated before we arrive, the faster we're loaded and the lower your bill, since you're paying by the hour. Loose stuff in drawers, photos off the walls, anything small enough to fit in your car — take a carload the day before. Does that make sense?' She even said she'd take her PCs herself and the response was 'Mm-hmm.' Also fix the hard mechanics: the hourly rate, mover/truck count, 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute increments were never spoken aloud on a call meant to close a quote, and No Worries never got named against her stated worry about mirrors, glass, and framed photos. Business flag for EMMA: she downsized the inventory verbally on this call (bed frame, cabinets, sofa, no appliances, no TV) and the estimate was never re-checked against it — that needs to be reconciled in the record before the twelfth or it becomes an estimate-accuracy miss either way. Follow-up action: she said she'd call back and nothing is scheduled, so the 9/12 8:30–9:00 slot is sitting unowned.
phone_presence_notes: Conversational and non-defensive under a price push, and the customer thanked him by name at the end, but the warmth was undercut by never using her name once, heavy disfluent run-ons, and answering his own 'how are you?' before she could reply.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily disfluent and garbled in places ('the insurance that hire evaluation that we provide,' 'as opposed to ten' where $210 was meant, 'the poppy, the your trucks Li, license number'), and the customer appears to be a non-native English speaker with fragmented lines, so clarity and pace cannot be fairly judged from text — audio is needed to tell rep delivery apart from transcription error.
